A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSPELL research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on four text-attributed graph datasets, expert ratings, perturbation tests, ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark, human-evaluation, ablation, and runtime results, with revisions to some reported values.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 replaces supporting nodes plus randomly selected neutral nodes under a size constraint with supporting nodes alone. It also explicitly describes sequential prompting of fixed-size batches. These are localized procedural revisions; the projector, hybrid prompts, and GSPELL+ objectives remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate node-classification explanations on CORA, WikiCS, LIAR, and the Amazon product subset, with human evaluation on CORA and Amazon. No dataset, task, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: v3 removes the text-only LLM comparator from the perturbation evaluation in Table 3, although it remains in other comparisons. Comparator membership in the main benchmark, architecture experiments, and human evaluation is otherwise unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 specifies 60%/20%/20% splits and 400 GCN training epochs; v3 Appendix D.1 specifies 60% training, 10% validation, 200 test nodes, and validation-selected training of 100–400 epochs. It also reports random Amazon subsampling, conflicting with the retained first-1000 description in Appendix B.1. These substantially revise reported protocols without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The perturbation analysis loses its text-only LLM control, reducing evidence about the contribution of projected embeddings to faithfulness. The token-count sensitivity results are revised at k=5. Architecture, LLM-backbone, component ablations, and example cases are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix D.1 newly specifies five random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting. Both versions already display uncertainty values in Tables 1–2 and average the Random baseline over five samples. The new disclosure does not demonstrate an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes GNNExplainer's Amazon fidelity from 94.8% to 94.5% and CORA size from 17.09 to 17.91. Table 3 changes Amazon GSPELL/GSPELL+ sizes from 2.3/1.8 to 4.25/4.24, revises CORA results, and removes the LLM row. Several k=5 ablation cells also change. These are reported revisions, not demonstrated gains under fixed experimental conditions.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 removes the formally defined randomized refinement and constant-size constraint. Section 4.1 corrects the LLM text-embedding dimension from R^k to R^h, and Section 3 explicitly links node features to a text encoder. No theorem or proof is added; the principal alignment and InfoNCE reasoning remains.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same central claims: explaining GNNs through projected embeddings and LLMs without fine-tuning either backbone, producing interpretable subgraphs, and balancing fidelity with sparsity. The conclusion's trade-off wording preserves this established contribution.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges lower baseline-relative fidelity instead of claiming a match, recommends Amazon k=5 rather than k=10, and adds qualifications about global context, inconsistent InfoNCE benefits, and over-trust. It also strengthens the comprehensiveness/random-drop comparison with GNNExplainer, although Table 3 does not support that superiority uniformly.

D1.justification: v3 adds substantial documentation of projector architecture, hyperparameter searches, temperature, default token count, generation settings, baseline implementations, and a two-hop computation-tree cap. It also identifies the human evaluators as authors. Conversely, v2's GPU specification and explicit GCN learning rate disappear. The code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The Kingma and Ba Adam reference is removed, and the baseline discussion drops the assertion that TAGExplainer is the only existing LLM explainer specifically for TAGs. The remaining cited literature and positioning around representation-aware explanations without an external explainer are retained.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting and reorganization affect the method and evaluation narrative. Metrics move into Section 5.1, perturbation evaluation joins Section 5.2, token-count and runtime analyses become Section 6, and the appendices are reorganized into datasets, extended experiments, implementation, and human evaluation. Future-work discussion is added.

P2.justification: The existing figures and tables are largely retained. Token-count and runtime tables move into the main text, table captions move below their displays, Table 2 reformats uncertainty values, and Table 3 loses a row and gains direction arrows. Figures 2–3 receive small prompt-label edits.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves implementation disclosure and presents more qualified interpretations, but introduces conflicting Amazon sampling descriptions and removes an informative LLM control from Table 3. Its support-only construction is also difficult to reconcile with retained ablations where post-processing enlarges subgraphs. These unresolved issues affect reproducibility and evidential strength, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
